tools.name: ink_create_base
tools.title: Scaffold Web Application Foundation
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Scaffold a complete, production-grade semantic web application foundation featuring OKLCH color token architecture, fluid typography scales, modern CSS logical properties, and bilingual Arabic RTL/LTR layout balance.

BEHAVIOR: Generates complete in-memory application files (index.html, styles.css, main.js) within the structured result envelope. Operates purely in-memory with zero direct filesystem side effects; callers receive the code ready to be written to disk. Requires no external credentials or elevated permissions.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: Call at the start of a web project to establish root HTML semantics, CSS custom property foundations, viewport meta tags, and font configurations.
- When NOT to use: Do NOT use to craft isolated UI widgets (use ink_craft_component instead) or to synthesize standalone color variables without project markup (use ink_generate_palette_tokens instead).
- Alternatives: Use ink_craft_component for individual components; use ink_generate_palette_tokens for standalone CSS color tokens.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope containing structured 'files' dictionary (index.html, styles.css, main.js), OKLCH tokensOverview, contrast verification analysis, and typography scales.

tools.name: ink_generate_palette_tokens
tools.title: Generate OKLCH Color Palette & Design Tokens
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Generate OKLCH palette ramps, semantic color tokens, fluid clamp() typography and modular spacing tokens with a complete WCAG 2.1 + APCA 0.98G contrast audit.

BEHAVIOR: Synthesizes CSS custom properties and typography/spacing steps purely in-memory (zero filesystem writes, zero network access). Colors are derived from perceptual ramps (equal OKLCH lightness increments or a configurable cubic-Bezier eased curve) and gamut mapped into the requested target (sRGB or Display P3). Every text x surface pairing (including muted text and elevated/subtle surfaces) plus accent/border UI pairings is measured on the EXPORTED 8-bit sRGB fallbacks using full-precision WCAG ratios; pass/fail decisions are never taken on a rounded value.

CONTRAST BEHAVIOUR: results are reported against the requested `contrastTarget` (AA/AAA/AA-Large/none). There is NO unconditional AAA guarantee. `correctionMode` may adjust a failing token's OKLCH lightness (hue and chroma preserved) and every adjustment is reported in `adjustments`. When a pairing cannot reach the target within the documented lightness limits, it is listed in `failedPairings` and the envelope status becomes 'partial' or 'blocked'.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: creating or refining a design system's color foundation, perceptual ramps, fluid typographic scales, or dark/light surface tokens.
- When NOT to use: extracting colors from an existing live website (use ink_inspect_website_style), scaffolding a project skeleton (use ink_create_base), or checking supplied colors (use ink_validate_design).
- Alternatives: ink_generate_fluid_scale for arbitrary clamp() values; ink_inspect_website_style to reverse-engineer existing sites.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope with gamut-mapped token map (`tokens`), per-token exports incl. sRGB fallbacks (`tokenExports`), perceptual ramps (`ramps`), the full contrast audit (`contrastAnalysis`), failed pairings, adjustments, typography/spacing scales and a ready-to-use :root stylesheet.

tools.description:
PURPOSE: Synthesize bespoke, tactile UI components (hero sections, glass cards, tactile buttons, navigation bars, metrics grids, modal dialogs) with semantic HTML5, modern CSS logical properties, and spring micro-interaction physics.

- When to use: Use when creating individual, high-craft UI components and interactive widgets that need to be embedded in an existing layout.

tools.description:
PURPOSE: Generate high-performance, responsive 3D WebGL scenes using Three.js (particle constellations, geometric wireframes, morphing meshes, or interactive hero canvases) with memory-safe lifecycles.

tools.name: ink_audit_security
tools.title: Audit Frontend Code Security & Headers
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Audit frontend and full-stack web code for client-side security vulnerabilities (DOM XSS, eval/Function sinks, innerHTML execution, plain-text token storage in localStorage, missing security headers, and strict CSP generation).

BEHAVIOR: Executes AST and regex static security scanning in-memory. Purely read-only; never executes or mutates the audited code, and never transmits source code over external networks. Emits severity ratings (critical, high, medium, low) and exact code remediations.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: Use prior to deployment or code review to ensure zero client-side injection vulnerabilities, secure token handling, and robust Content-Security-Policy headers.
- When NOT to use: Do NOT use to validate CSS aesthetic quality, color contrast, or fluid typography rules (use ink_validate_design instead), nor for external URL penetration testing.
- Alternatives: Use ink_validate_design for design system, contrast, and bidi compliance checks; use ink_run_python_tests for Python AST test suites.

tools.name: ink_validate_design
tools.title: Validate Design Craft & Contrast Compliance
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Evaluate HTML and CSS against anti-AI-slop heuristics, measure WCAG 2.1 contrast on the supplied color pair, report APCA 0.98G contrast, and audit RTL/LTR logical properties and optical centering.

BEHAVIOR: Executes in-memory static analysis on the supplied code strings. Completely read-only with zero filesystem writes, no network requests, and deterministic scoring. Contrast is computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula on the FULL-PRECISION ratio: pass/fail booleans use the exact ratio while the displayed `ratio` value is rounded to two decimals, so a pair such as #148700 on #000000 (exact 4.4953, displayed 4.50) correctly FAILS normal-text AA. APCA uses the reference 0.98G equations (APCA-specific luminance, black soft clamp, polarity exponents, low-contrast clipping and offsets) with no arbitrary output clamp.

FLAGS: `checkBidi` toggles the logical-property audit. `checkCentering` toggles the optical centering / horizontal overflow audit (centered body copy, 100vw overflow, oversized fixed widths, auto margins without max-width, over-tight tracking); when disabled the audit is skipped and reported as null. `textFontSizePx`/`textFontWeight` enable font-size/weight-aware APCA guidance from the published lookup table (APCA font lookup, Public Beta 0.1.7 (G); basis "apca-0.1.7-G-lookup"). `textUse` ("large" by default; "body" applies APCA's documented +15 Lc adjustment below Lc 70; "non-text" uses the raw Lc) selects the table row, weights snap to the nearest published column, and the 999/777 sentinel codes never pass for real text.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: after creating or modifying layouts, components, or stylesheets to verify craft quality, contrast compliance, bidi readiness, and centering before committing.
- When NOT to use: JavaScript security scanning (ink_audit_security), browser screenshots (ink_capture_viewport), or whole-system audits (ink_generate_palette_tokens).
- Alternatives: ink_audit_security for security/XSS checks; ink_capture_viewport for visual verification.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope containing 'craftScore', 'craftGrade', 'isHighCraft', 'antiSlopChecks', the exact/displayed 'contrast' report with WCAG flags and APCA guidance, 'bidiAndAlignment', 'centeringAudit' and prioritized 'remediationAdvice'.

tools.name: ink_run_python_tests
tools.title: Run Python Verification Suite (AST, Contrast, APCA, Capture)
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Execute the external Python verification suite for AST static analysis, WCAG + APCA 0.98G contrast maths, design heuristics, bidi auditing, website inspection and headless layout capture.

BEHAVIOR: Spawns the local Python 3 ink_verifier engine in a subprocess and returns its structured JSON. This tool is NOT read-only and NOT closed-world: the 'capture' action WRITES PNG/SVG snapshot files to disk, and the 'inspect' action FETCHES a remote URL. Both facts are reflected in the tool annotations (readOnlyHint: false, openWorldHint: true). Requires Python 3.10+ on PATH (override with INK_PYTHON_PATH). The optional `target` parameter is forwarded to the Python engine for the 'inspect' and 'capture' actions.

CONTRAST BEHAVIOUR: the Python engine classifies WCAG compliance from the FULL-PRECISION ratio (`ratio_exact`) and only rounds the displayed `ratio`, matching the TypeScript engine. The `contrast` action also reports APCA 0.98G computed with the reference equations. Unsupported color syntax is reported as an error instead of silently resolving to black.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: deep multi-pass Python analysis, independent contrast/APCA verification, remote site inspection, or real-browser snapshots.
- When NOT to use: fast in-memory CSS validation without Python (ink_validate_design) or standalone client-side security audits (ink_audit_security).
- Alternatives: ink_validate_design for TypeScript-native verification; ink_capture_viewport for the wrapped snapshot workflow.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope whose `data` contains the structured outcome of the invoked action ('contrast', 'security', 'visual', 'audit', 'full', 'bidi', 'inspect', 'capture').

tools.name: ink_capture_viewport
tools.title: Capture Multi-Viewport Responsive Snapshots
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Capture viewport snapshots (16:9 desktop landscape, 9:16 vertical story, and 390x844 mobile) via headless Chromium to verify layout integrity, responsiveness, and optical centering.

BEHAVIOR: Launches a local headless browser with an isolated temporary user-data profile, renders the provided HTML string or URL, and WRITES one image file per viewport into `outputDirectory` (default '.ink_snapshots/'). When no browser is installed it writes deterministic SVG fallbacks and reports `format`. This tool therefore writes files and can fetch remote URLs (annotations: readOnlyHint false, openWorldHint true). Browser capture needs a longer timeout than the default 12s, because three sequential headless renders are performed.

ERROR BEHAVIOUR: backend failures are returned as proper MCP error results (`isError: true`) that preserve the underlying Python error message instead of being reshaped into an output-schema validation error.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: after making HTML/CSS modifications or finishing a component to visually confirm alignment across desktop, mobile, and tall vertical screens.
- When NOT to use: fast code syntax or contrast checks without browser rendering (ink_validate_design).
- Alternatives: ink_validate_design for fast static design linting; ink_inspect_website_style to reverse-engineer design tokens.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope with a 'snapshots' list (label, viewport, exact dimensions, file path, size, format) and layout overflow metrics.

tools.name: ink_inspect_website_style
tools.title: Inspect & Reverse-Engineer Website Style
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Deconstruct existing live websites or HTML/CSS templates to reverse-engineer color palettes, typography scales, elevation shadows, and layout DNA into modern OKLCH tokens.

BEHAVIOR: Fetches public website markup over HTTPS (10s timeout, redirect limits, private-subnet blocking) or parses local HTML/CSS in-memory. Strictly read-only with zero disk modifications. `extractOklchPalette` is applied to BOTH paths: every extracted hex, rgb()/rgba() and oklch() literal is converted with real color math (sRGB -> linear -> OKLab -> OKLCH) and gamut mapped for the requested target. Literals that cannot be converted are reported in `unsupportedColors` instead of being replaced by a fixed palette, and the recommended token block is derived from the actual extracted colors.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: analyzing a reference website or mockup to extract its visual hierarchy, typography system, and color ramps.
- When NOT to use: generating novel color tokens from scratch (ink_generate_palette_tokens) or evaluating code for anti-slop compliance (ink_validate_design).
- Alternatives: ink_generate_palette_tokens to synthesize new design tokens; ink_capture_viewport to capture visual snapshots.

tools.name: ink_generate_gradient
tools.title: Generate Perceptual OKLCH/OKLab Gradient
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Interpolate a perceptual multi-stop gradient in OKLCH or OKLab space with CSS Color 4 gamut mapping and independent sRGB/Display P3 exports.

BEHAVIOR: Computes stops purely in-memory (zero filesystem writes, zero network access, deterministic output). Either two endpoints (`fromOklch`/`toOklch` plus an integer `steps`) or an authored `stops` array with explicit positions and optional alpha. `steps` must be an integer - fractional counts are rejected instead of silently floored. Stop positions are validated (finite, within [0,1], non-decreasing). Alpha below 1 switches to premultiplied interpolation so transparent stops do not produce dark halos. CSS interpolation is always explicit: `linear-gradient(<direction> in oklch|oklab, ...)`. Stops are gamut mapped with the CSS Color 4 binary-search local-MINDE algorithm; the target-gamut CSS and an INDEPENDENT sRGB fallback are both emitted, and Display P3 channels are never encoded as #rrggbb.

GAMUT POLICY: gamut validation is SAMPLED at `gamutValidationSamples` uniform positions. Passing samples do not prove every point of the continuous gradient is in gamut; the returned `gamut` object states the policy, sample count and whether any sample required chroma reduction.

CSS OUTPUT: stop positions are serialized whenever they differ from the implicit even spacing (so authored two-stop positions such as 20%/80% survive), the hue interpolation method is always written (`in oklch shorter hue` / `longer hue` / `increasing hue` / `decreasing hue`), and alpha is written INSIDE the color function (`oklch(L C H / A)`, `color(display-p3 r g b / A)`). Transparency uses CSS Color 4 premultiplied interpolation in the selected space: for polar OKLCH the hue is not premultiplied, so equal-alpha polar stops keep their chroma and hue arc.

CONTRAST POLICY: WCAG/APCA are defined on opaque colors, so transparent stops are alpha-composited over `contrastBackdropHex` (default #ffffff) before measuring. The report states the backdrop, the composited background, the opaque gradient color and the interpolated alpha per sample.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: smooth brand gradients, background ramps, or accent transitions with authored stop positions and transparency.
- When NOT to use: scaffolding projects (ink_create_base), token systems (ink_generate_palette_tokens), or one-off contrast checks (ink_validate_design).
- Alternatives: ink_generate_palette_tokens for full token systems; ink_generate_spacing_scale for layout rhythm.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope with `stops` (dual-gamut export data per stop), `css`, `cssSrgb`, `cssP3`, `hexes`, the sampled `gamut` report and - when `contrastForegroundHex` is supplied - a contrast report with every sample, the compositing context and the reported worst case.

alpha.description: Stop alpha in [0, 1]; below 1 switches interpolation to premultiplied mode

stops.description: Authored stop list with explicit positions (2-16). Overrides fromOklch/toOklch when provided.

steps.description: Number of interpolated stops (integer 2-16). Fractional values are rejected, not floored.

tools.name: ink_generate_spacing_scale
tools.title: Generate Fluid Spacing Scale
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Generate a modular spacing scale (size(n) = basePx * ratio^n) with px/rem and optional fluid clamp() tokens.

BEHAVIOR: Computes spacing steps purely in-memory from a base size and modular ratio, optionally emitting fluid clamp() tokens scaled between minVw and maxVw. Zero filesystem writes and zero network access; deterministic output for identical inputs. The nine-step 3xs..3xl preset remains the default, and `steps`/`stepCount` allow a custom range or name list. The fluid lower bound is configurable through `fluidMinFactor` (default 0.85) and rem conversion honours `rootFontPx`.

VALIDATION: `basePx` must be a finite number > 0; `ratio` must be a finite number >= 1 (a decreasing scale is rejected unless explicitly allowed); when `fluid` is true both viewports must be positive with maxVw > minVw; `fluidMinFactor` must lie in (0, 1]. Invalid input fails fast with an explicit message instead of emitting NaN/Infinity CSS.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: establishing layout rhythm, gap tokens, or padding scales for a design system.
- When NOT to use: color tokens (ink_generate_palette_tokens), gradients (ink_generate_gradient), or arbitrary fluid clamps (ink_generate_fluid_scale).
- Alternatives: ink_generate_fluid_scale for one-off clamp() values; ink_generate_palette_tokens for a combined color+spacing system.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope with the `tokens` scale map (px/rem/clamp/fluidMinPx/step index), a ready-to-paste CSS ':root' block, and the resolved scale parameters.

tools.name: ink_generate_fluid_scale
tools.title: Generate Fluid Clamp Scale
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Generate arbitrary CSS fluid clamp() values from explicit minimum/maximum sizes and viewport bounds.

BEHAVIOR: Uses the exact linear formula slope = (maxSize - minSize) / (maxViewport - minViewport), intercept = minSize - minViewport * slope, serialized as clamp(minSize/root rem, intercept/root rem + slope*100 vw, maxSize/root rem). Purely in-memory: zero filesystem writes, zero network access, deterministic output. `rootFontPx` is configurable (default 16), so non-16px roots are handled correctly.

VALIDATION: every numeric input must be finite; sizes and viewports must be > 0; maxViewportPx must be strictly greater than minViewportPx (equal or reversed bounds are rejected instead of producing `-Infinityrem + Infinityvw`); every entry must satisfy maxPx >= minPx. Invalid input fails fast with an explicit message, so invalid CSS can never be generated.

USAGE GUIDELINES:
- When to use: one-off fluid sizing (fluid hero type, fluid spacing, fluid radii) or verifying the endpoint accuracy of a clamp.
- When NOT to use: whole type scales (ink_generate_palette_tokens with includeTypography, or ink_create_base) or complete spacing scales (ink_generate_spacing_scale).
- Alternatives: ink_generate_spacing_scale for modular spacing; ink_generate_palette_tokens for a full token system.

RETURNS: ResultEnvelope with one `values` entry per token (slope, intercept, clampCss and the measured endpoint values/errors), a ready-to-paste :root CSS block and the documented endpoint tolerance.
